name: steam_reheat_power_plant
title: Steam power plant with reheat (Cengel exercise 10-34)
summary: Steady reheat Rankine cycle on water: saturated liquid is pumped from 10 kPa to 10 MPa, boiled to 500 °C, expanded to 1 MPa, reheated once to 500 °C and expanded to 10 kPa. For an imposed net power of 80 MW the model returns the thermal efficiency and the steam mass flow.

origin.course: KU Leuven thermodynamics; textbook exercise Cengel 10-34

verification.summary: Compared with the solution stored in 10-34.EES (compare_solution.py, no unit scaling): 37 common variables, one above rtol 0.001. Largest relative difference 1.26e-03 is T_6 (88.084 °C vs 87.973 °C), from CoolProp versus EES steam properties plus a 687 J/kg enthalpy difference. Enthalpies and entropies stay within 4.62e-04. Net power 80 MW, efficiency 0.3405, steam flow 62.65 kg/s.
verification.reference: EES stored solution of 10-34.EES (compare_solution.py, units already SI)
verification.notes: Summary line: 37 common variables, 1 differ (rtol=0.001); only in EES: 0; only in CoolSolve: 0. T_6 is the only variable above rtol 0.001. At the stored h_6, CoolSolve returns 87.724 °C against the stored 87.973 °C; the solved h_6 is 687 J/kg higher and raises T by about 0.36 °C, leaving +0.111 °C. Liquid enthalpies differ by about 87 J/kg and vapour enthalpies by 550 to 1130 J/kg; entropies by 0.30 J/kg-K (liquid) to about 2.5 J/kg-K (vapour). Not a reference-state offset. Equation residuals are at most 6.41e-10. The ees_variables.csv units column is empty and the stored enthalpies are already in J, so --ees-units was not used.
